learnerStatement: Simulated learner. This review finds problems; it is not evidence that anyone learned.
learnerBoundary: Everyday numeracy, simple charts, comparison of numbers and familiar household objects; no domain-specific theory assumed.

observations.prediction: Selected two ohms and locked it in.
observations.exploration: Baseline one metre/one millimetre gave one ohm. Length End three metres gave three ohms at original diameter. At2.5 metres/0.25 mm gave forty ohms and area0.063. Set asked two metres/0.5 mm: eight ohms and quarter area. Length Home0.5 metres at same diameter gave two ohms; one metre gave four. Restored two metres and eight.
observations.reveal: Corrected to eight, combined length factor two and diameter-squared area factor quarter, gave R equals resistivity times length divided by area. Same metal and temperature conditions explicit; baseline resistance illustrative rather than copper value.
observations.visual: Actual dark1257 by936 screenshots inspected. Side and end-on wire views, dashed original dimensions and length/area/resistance chips matched. Thickness exaggeration disclosed; reveal text legible.
observations.previewIsolation: Preview banner said history and analytics are not saved.
observations.blinding: No source, builder notes or other reviews inspected.

prediction.reason: Concrete combined-scale prediction targets ignoring diameter-squared area.
prediction.evidence: Two versus four versus eight ohms.

interaction.reason: Independent length and diameter states separate linear and squared contributions.
interaction.evidence: One-metre half-diameter four ohms; two-metre half-diameter eight.

payoff.reason: Reveal explains product of two mechanisms with model conditions.
payoff.evidence: Length times two and area quarter yields resistance times eight.

clarity.reason: End-on view and area chip clarify width versus cross-section.
clarity.evidence: Thickness exaggeration and illustrative material baseline explicit.

transfer.reason: General formula and conditions supplied without a new application.

accessibility.evidence: Keyboard sliders worked; screen reader, contrast and reduced motion unaudited.

surprise.reason: Halving width multiplies resistance fourfold before length change.

visualExplanation.reason: End-on circle and dashed baseline reveal squared-area change.

playfulness.reason: Two geometric sliders update wire and numbers.

practicalValue.reason: Clarifies conductor geometry effects under fixed material conditions.
practicalValue.evidence: Length and cross-section determine modeled resistance.

depth.reason: Combines direct and inverse geometric scaling.

complexity.reason: Simple controls introduce area scaling and resistance relation.
complexity.conceptualDemand: Separate diameter from area and multiply independent scaling factors.
complexity.notationRepresentationBurden: Metres,millimetres,ohms, Greek rho and formula ratios.

whyCool: A small diameter change has a squared effect before the longer wire adds its own cost.
caveat: Fixed metal and temperature assumed; resistance baseline is explicitly illustrative.
effort: Approximately 3 minutes of actual browser review.
